name: 1 Pontypool Place
description: Tour of home & garden designed in 2018 by Nagan Johnson Architects
address: 1 Pontypool Place London London, Greater London, SE1 8QF

name: 141 Coldershaw Road, W13
description: The home of Eric and Jessica Huntley , community activists and educators who founded the pioneering company Bogle-L'Ouverture Publications in 1968, lived and ran their bookshop from this semi detached property soon after.  The house is a Black British cultural archivists dream; filled with books, arts and craft and correspondence from the 1960s to the present day.

name: 60 Years of the BT Tower: Signals and Sightlines
description: 60 years on from the opening of the BT Tower, and amidst its sale to a hotel consortium, participants are invited on a research-led walk around Fitzrovia to reflect on the hidden stories and unseen infrastructures that contribute to the creation of the city and its green spaces.
address: The Building Centre, 26 Store Street, WC1E 7BT

name: Andaz London Liverpool Street
description:
Andaz London Liverpool Street, a concept by Hyatt, blends rich history dating back to the 1200s with modern decor and the vibrant energy of its London neighborhood.

Step inside and join us for an open house tour led by our dedicated team!

name: Barnard's Inn Hall
description: Barnard's Inn in Holborn dates back to the mid-13th century. It is now the home of Gresham College which has been providing free public lectures since 1597. Over the centuries it has been a law school and home to the Mercers' School. Notable architectural elements include 15th-century wooden bays, 16th-century linen fold wood panelling, and has the only surviving crown posts in Greater London.

name: Bodney Road Studios
description: Bodney Road Studio's is home to a range of practitioners working in the built environment including architectural photographer Lorenzo Zandri, graphic designers Polytechnic and place futurists The Place Bureau. Join us on 19–20 September when we will open the studios in conjunction with a programme of exhibitions and events by Lorenzo Zandri, Polytechnic, Sammi Gale and The Place Bureau.

name: Borough Yards: Panel discussion
description: Borough Yards is a vibrant cultural and retail quarter at the heart of London Bridge’s culinary and creative scenes. Set within historic railway arches and revived Victorian streets, Borough Yards is a neighbourhood designed to bring people together through shops, restaurants, pop-ups and year-round cultural programming.

name: Boston Manor House
description: Boston Manor House is a Jacobean House built for Lady Mary Reade in 1623 and later owned by the Clitherow family from the 1670s until the 1920s. The House is now open to the public with free entry six days a week. Its beautifully restored historic interiors, including breath-taking ornate plasterwork, are joined by two community exhibition galleries, meeting rooms and an attractive modern café.
address: Boston Manor House, Boston Manor Road, Brentford, TW8 9JX

name: Burlington House: Linnean Society of London
description: The world's oldest active biological society. Founded in 1788, the Society takes its name from the Swedish naturalist Carl Linnaeus whose botanical, zoological and library collections have been in its keeping since 1829.

name: Burlington House: Society of Antiquaries of London
description: The Society of Antiquaries of London has been exploring the material past since the early eighteenth century. In the 1870s, the Society set up home in purpose-built grade II* listed apartments in Burlington House, with a grand galleried library housing 130,000 books. Today's membership of 3,000 Fellows are leading experts in archaeology, history, art, architecture, and heritage.

name: Common Edge: Art, Community and Protest in Wanstead and Leytonstone
description: This walk explores how artists, activists and local communities have contested, defended and reimagined urban space across Wanstead Flats and Leytonstone. From the struggle to protect common land and Epping Forest to the creative resistance of the M11 protests and contemporary grassroots projects, we uncover histories of collective action, cultural imagination and alternative visions for the city.

name: Conway Hall
description: The home of Conway Hall Ethical Society, an organisation renowned as a hub for progressive thought. Grade II listed building with both Arts and Crafts and Art Deco features adding to its distinctive style.

name: County Hall Kingston
description:
London Square presents a rare opportunity to live within the sensitively restored former Surrey County Hall, complemented by a striking collection of contemporary new-build homes and commercial areas for hire.

Set in the heart of Kingston, residents enjoy a riverside town rich in culture, green spaces, shopping and dining - all with excellent connection to London and beyond.

name: Croydon Urban Room
description: The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action.

name: Designed to be forgotten: women in South Kensington
description:
On this  walk you will see some of the forgotten contributions of Victorian women to the magnificent buildings of South Kensington, in particular the V&A and the Royal Albert Hall. 

You will also see how women were represented very differently from men on the buildings and memorials of this internationally important arts and science district.
address: Outside the V&A Exhibition Road Entrance, Exhibition Road, SW7 2PA

name: Destination Battersea
description: This tour explores the evolution of Battersea, with a particular focus on its role as a destination for Londoners. From the days of the Red House Tavern, through the post-war Festival of Britain's Pleasure Gardens, to the modern-day Battersea Power Station, this stretch of London along the River Thames has long offered opportunities for leisure, entertainment, and discovery.
address: Battersea Park Railway Station, Battersea Park Road, Nine Elms

name: E.ON's Citigen energy centre
description: Hidden behind two Listed Building facades opposite Smithfield Market, and spread across eight floors below and above ground, E.ON's Citigen energy centre produces electricity, heat and cooling to buildings across the Square Mile.

name: Eastbury Manor House
description: One of the finest surviving Elizabethan red brick Manor houses- Grade I listed. Contains 17th Century wall-paintings, charming walled garden and a fine Tudor tower with original stairs. Many original features have been restored and layout remains mostly unchanged in over 400 years.
address: Eastbury Manor House, Eastbury Square, Barking, IG11 9SN

name: Explore the authentically recreated Colony Room
description: A revival and love letter to London’s lost bohemia. Travel back in time to the legendary haunt of some of Soho's greatest creatives.   Featuring pictures, press cuttings and even the piano from the much loved private members club.

name: Fitzrovia Chapel
description: Loughborough Pearson's red brick building is unimposing from the outside, but inside is a riot of Gothic Revival design. Golden mosaics reveal the character of the Grade II* listed chapel, built as part of the Middlesex Hospital.

name: Fleet Street Heritage Wall and Sundial
description: The Fleet Street Heritage Wall comprises 86 A3 information panels about the people, places, ideas and newspapers which made the name o Fleet Street famous throughout the world.  From 17th to 20th Sept frequent talks will be given on thesundial and the Heritage Wall, and its innovative design features which will  mqke it accessible to all comers through web pages, Easy Read pages, and audio files

name: From Forest to Morris: A walk around Walthamstow
description: A walk around historic Walthamstow showing how this unique area grew from a village into a thriving suburb, its social history and the variety of buildings that can be found where Epping Forest meets William Morris.
address: Outside Costa Coffee at Walthamstow Central Station 5 Station Approac

name: From bomb site to blueprint: walking the rebuilt City
description: Laying Blitz photographs against the streets of today, this tour traces the rebuilding of the City around St Paul's from rival postwar blueprints to pocket parks and privately-owned public spaces. We look at what today’s business district replaced and also at the remnants of conflict still visible in the streets today.
address: Statue of Queen Anne, St. Paul's Churchyard, EC4M 8AY

name: Garage Gallery E17
description: In 2022 we created an art gallery in the garage below our house in a residential street in Walthamstow village.   We aim to bring art into our community, acting as a resource to support artists on a not-for-profit basis.  By the time of Open House we will have hosted 26 exhibitions in a wide range of media, by both emerging and more experienced artists.

name: Green Lodge
description: Green Lodge is a low-energy family home by Stylus Architects, carefully embedded into the landscape of Putney Heath. Much of the accommodation is concealed below ground, allowing the building to maintain a modest presence whilst bringing natural light into every room through a series of lightwells and rooflights.

name: Herne Hill Velodrome
description:
Herne Hill Velodrome, opened in 1891, hosted track cycling events for the 1948 Olympics, is now home to a thriving grassroots cycling facility - hosting everything from Learn to Cycle to local and international racing events. 
HHV overcame the threat of closure in the early 2000s, and a new pavilion, designed by Mike Taylor of Hopkins Architects, opened in 2017.

name: Hounslow House
description: The London Borough of Hounslow's 2019 contemporary home designed by Sheppard Robson, with iconic iridescent façade and public and private spaces stitched together by a bold and sculptural staircase, is open for architectural tours led by Hounslow Council's Culture team.

name: IMPACT Community Arts Centre
description: We are a theatre company for performers and artists with learning disabilities in the West London area. We will put on an exhibition of artworks and costumes at our Community Arts Centre.
address: Ealing Central Sports Ground, Horsenden Lane South, Greenford

name: Ibraaz
description: Ibraaz is a London-based cultural institution for art, ideas, and dialogue from the Global Majority. Bringing together artists, thinkers, and communities through exhibitions, film, debate, publishing, and multidisciplinary programming, Ibraaz creates a brave space where culture fosters exchange, pluralism, and shared humanity.

name: JCDecaux UK – Tour & Presentation
description: JCDecaux, the world’s largest Out-of-Home advertising company, invites you inside its iconic Grade II listed HQ for a special event. The morning will feature a talk by local historian James Marshall, an overview of the building’s restoration and adaptation by Foster + Partners in 1997 with sensitive preservation of its period frontage, and a tour of its architecturally designed street furniture.
address: 991 Great West Road, Brentford, Middlesex, TW8 9DN

name: Jewish Westminster
description: Ths walk will look at the history of Jewish Communities in England, starting with the medieval period through to the expulsion in 1290 and redmission under Oliver Cromwell in 1656. It will also look at some of the Jewish people living as Christians between these times and the key contributions Jews have made to many of the key landmarks in London  as well as England's political life.
address: Charing Cross Station - Eleanor Cross, WC2N 5HS

name: London National Park City Visitors Centre
description: London is the world's first National Park City, and our visitors centre at 80 Mortimer Street is the entry point to hundreds of places to visit and things to do across a greener, healthier and wilder London.

name: London Open Form Pavilion of Air
description: A floating acoustic architecture, playfully reframing public space as an essential community engagement through sound & site mapping. Accessed by smartphone, headphones & echoes.xyz app, the Pavilion is located outside the Serpentine Gallery,. Drawing on Oskar & Zofia Hansen’s Open Form architectural concept it is one of 15 in a series including Venice, Berlin, Dublin, Bergen and Arctic Norway.

name: Lorenzo Zandri - Urban Narrative
description: During the festival, Lorenzo Zandri’s studio transforms into an immersive environment that bridges the gap between architectural theory and photographic practice. Eschewing traditional construction to focus on the 'process of the image’, Zandri will present an analytical overview of his practice and research – where photography serves as a tool for urban narrative rather than mere documentation.
address: Bodney Road Studios, 1 Bodney Road, Unit 2, E8 1AY

name: Memorial Community Church
description: Formerly known as Memorial Baptist Church this Grade II listed building opened in 1922, it retains many original features. Open House will include access to the church, gallery and bell tower, and information on church history. 18th September at 7pm Lydia Thornley will lead a talk on the craft skills used in the building, and on the 19th 3.30-6pm there is a sketching workshop

name: Morris+Company | 'Waste Not: Materials, Making and the Circular Economy' Exhibition
description: Morris+Company is an award-winning architecture practice based in Hackney, east London. We have applied circular economy principles to the retrofit of our own studio, gallery and café space on Mare Street, reducing waste, reusing materials, and designing for longevity.  We place the creative ‘act’ of architecture onto the high street, reveal our practice to the public and engage local communities.

name: Museum of Croydon Behind the Scenes Tour
description:
Explore the Museum of Croydon and Croydon Archives:

- Join the Curator of the Museum of Croydon and the Borough Archivist of the Croydon Archives on an intimate guided tour of our stored, rarely seen collections.
- Explore our current exhibitions with our expert staff, including Grayson Perry's Essex House Tapestries and a brand-new exhibition on Croydon's Architecture

name: North Lambeth: Architecture, state and society
description: This architecture and open-space tour explores post-war north Lambeth. Born in an era of optimism for health, housing, learning, and play, these modernist places tell a deeper story. We will look at the people of influence, reflect on representation, and how culture continues to challenge. By considering people, place and context we shall revisit what matters in making a city for all.
address: St Thomas' Hospital Garden, Westminster Bridge Rd, SE1 7GA

name: Ongéan
description:
Ongéan Ecosystem : 
Art Studios, Gallery, Performance Space, Edible Garden & Kitchen. All built and designed with 99% Reclaimed Materials by artist Adam Ge-Saelis.
address: Ongéan, Park Mews, Croxted rd, SE24 9DB

name: Our Yard at Clitterhouse Farm
description: Come and visit this grassroots community enterprise where old meets new in the form of the historic farm buildings alongside our crowdfunded cafe. Find out how some of these historic buildings have been saved and lovingly bought back into community use, and find out about our future plans.
address: Clitterhouse Playing Fields, Claremont Rd, NW2 1AP

name: Past Forward: Where Heritage Meets Innovation | Open studios at DIA
description: Discover an exhibition exploring innovation in heritage through projects and stories with Donald Insall Associates. A curated display and film reveal how design, research and conservation are reshaping historic environments. Visit their Grade II-listed Edwardian studio (1914, Sydney Tatchell).

name: People's Museum Somers Town
description:
A great little museum set in the Grade 2 listed Ossulston Estate - a prime example of pre-war Social housing - based on Karl Marz Hof in Vienna.
Open Tuesday to Saturday 10am-5pm, plus Sunday 13th 12am-4pm.

name: Poroban studio
description: Poroban will open their studio to the public, where our team will be available to discuss sustainable construction and view samples - including a range of UK grown timbers.  Currently in development is the new Hastings Castle Visitor Centre, that follows 'Design for Dissassembly' principles, and a house extension built in Glulam timber, UK grown Sweet Chestnut and English Poplar.

name: Preedy Glass
description: An industrial building originally built for maintaining railways with a modern rear extension now housing a modern glass processing company

name: Red House
description: The only house commissioned, created and lived in by William Morris, founder of the Arts and Crafts movement. Much original detail survives, decorated  by the Pre-Raphaelites, and of extraordinary architectural and social significance.

name: Refugees at Home at International House
description:
For one day only, the charity Refugees at Home is holding a special photography exhibition at their home, International House. 

'Home Between Homes: The Faces Behind Hosting' showcases the stories of ordinary people who have opened their own homes to refugees.

name: Resonance FM Studios
description: Resonance FM is a pioneering, non-profit community radio station, with a studio at 7 Risborough Street, Southwark, London. Broadcasting 24/7 on 104.4 FM, DAB, and online, it offers over 100 weekly shows created by volunteer engineers and programme-makers. The station champions free expression and artistic diversity, providing a platform for local and international voices across arts & culture.

name: Romanian Cultural Institute
description: Situated in one of the largest and grandest 19th century squares in London, 1 Belgrave Square was acquired by Romania in 1936 and is now home to the Romanian Cultural Institute.

name: Secrets and Symbols of the City
description:
A curious and enlightening wander through the City of London led by an expert guide. If you know where to look, the past still communicates its secrets concealed within a city that is 2000 years old.

We'll discover clues to the City’s past in strange marks and curious symbols along the route, keeping an eye out for honeybees, demi-maidens and sunbursts.
address: City Information Centre, St Paul's Churchyard, EC4M 8BX

name: Soho - forever changing
description: The area post 1700 became very cosmopolitan with immigrants mainly from Europe, and their influence on food and drink became increasingly important. This tour is based on food and drink, passing by restaurants, pubs, coffee bars,  pâtisserie and  delis that have been present for decades, finishing at a relatively new site.
address: Opposite Coach and Horses , Greek street/ Romilly Street, W1D 5DH

name: Southlands Arts Centre
description: Explore Southlands Arts Centre and discover the history and architecture of this Grade II listed Queen Anne-style building. Admire its distinctive red-brick façade, elegant decorative detailing and historic interiors, and learn how this former private residence has evolved into a thriving community arts centre, celebrating Hillingdon's rich architectural and cultural heritage.
address: Southlands Arts Centre, 75, The Green, West Drayton, UB7 7PW

name: St Alban the Martyr, South Norwood
description: Since 1891, St Alban's has served South Norwood and Thornton Heath; areas that began to develop with the coming of the railways. The church  was  built by the community and is  still serving the community.  The building design altered considerably from start to finish and a small exhibition will give examples of the various suggestions.

name: St Anne's Church, Kew Green
description: St Anne's Church, Kew Green was consecrated in 1714. Built with the support of Queen Anne it has been a place of worship for the Royal Families over the centuries. The original 'chapel' has been extended many times and the church is now a little known gem in South West London with a fascinating past.

name: St Anne's Church, Limehouse
description: St Anne's Limehouse has been described as 'the finest parish church in England.' Designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor, it is Grade I listed and one of the Major Churches in the Church of England. It is home to a thriving Christian congregation.

name: St Bride's Church, Fleet Street
description: Wren designed building of 1675, interior lost in blitz of 1940, reopened 1957 with 'Wren inspired' interior
address: St Bride's Church, St Bride's Avenue, EC4Y 8AU

name: St Lawrence
description: St Lawrence started life as a hospital and chapel in the 12th century. There is a 15th century tower but the rest of the building was rebuilt in the 19th century. It was unused and  virtually derelict since the 1960s.  It has been refurbished but is currently empty. We will not have access to the interior.

name: St Mary & St Joseph Roman Catholic Church, Poplar
description: Grade II Listed.   Designed by Adrian Gilbert Scott.  Cruciform shape (120 feet by 120 feet) of steel girder and brick construction. Its Lantern tower – based on Ely Cathedral – is supported on parabolic arches 35 feet wide and 50 feet high.  The Stained Glass Windows were designed by John Wilson of Edinburgh and the Stations of the Cross  carved in Blue Horton Stone by Peter Watts.
address: St Mary & St Joseph Church, Upper North Street, Poplar, London

name: St Mary's Church, Battersea
description: During Open House, the Friends of Battersea Parish Church present a Floral Festival, organ recitals, historical displays, alongside 3 talks exploring history, creativity, sanctuary & Battersea’s radical past. Sat 12 Sept Dr. Peter Rumley at 6pm, Tues 15 Guy Stagg at 6.30pm,  Thurs 17 at 6.30pm Rory Walsh & Mike Squires.  Plus Join us for Choral Evensong amidst the flowers at St Mary’s Battersea.

name: St Pancras Church & Crypt
description: The church (1822 - Grade I listed) is an early and important example of Greek Revival architecture in London. Significant features include the caryatids and tower copied from models in Athens, and the atmospheric crypt.
address: Euston Road/Upper Woburn Place NW1, NW1 2BA

name: Streets of change: growing up in North Kensington
description: Unpack my story of North Kensington’s rich history on this guided walk. My family was one of the first families to move into the Brutalist-style Trellick Tower. From rural roots to industrial hub, class divides to cultural revolution – discover hidden stories, iconic sites, and how migration and activism shaped a vibrant, ever-changing community like no other: my childhood playground.
address: Outside Loaf Shop, 103 Lancaster Road, W11 1QN

name: String House - Camberwell
description: Contemporary timber frame home with unique string screen; a postwar house reassembled to follow passive house principles. The structure was built in 7 weeks to create a reimagined flexible home of two halves enabling an Airbnb rental that bypasses the first floor kitchen & living area, located to borrow views towards mature trees at the rear & city buses to the front expanding senses & spaces.

name: Swakeleys Estate
description: A most important house in Ickenham, an outstanding example of Jacobean architecture built in the 1630s. Red brick construction laid in English bond on an H plan. Great Hall includes the 1655 Harrington Screen, 18C marble fireplace panelling.
address: Swakeleys Road, Ickenham (access from Milton Road) , UB10 8LD

name: The Clockworks
description: The Clockworks is the only museum in the world dedicated to electrical horology. A major collection of clocks and timekeepers charts the development of networked and precision timekeeping, from 1840-1970, while an onsite workshop showcases modern and heritage clock conservation in action.

name: The Gaumont State Theatre
description: The Gaumont State Theatre in Kilburn, London, reopened for a live concert on 6 November 2025 for the first time in almost 50 years. Now a church, the former 4,004-seat super cinema welcomed a near-capacity audience for a performance by the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra and guest singers.

name: The King's Foundation - Charlotte Road
description: A refurbished factory warehouse, the repurposed space now hosts educational programmes and activities of the School of Traditional Arts and the architectural team of the King’s Foundation. Live demonstrations of traditional arts skills by students and alumni, scheduled talks on KF's architectural projects, and guided tours all await the visitor.

name: The Literary City
description: A walking tour of the City, visiting key areas associated with famous writers, from Shakespeare, Dr Johnson, Oscar Wilde, and many others.
address: St Mary Aldemanbury Garden, Love Lane, EC2P 2NQ

name: The Purpose of Light: Exhibition by Misan Harriman
description: The Purpose of Light, Misan Harriman’s landmark photographic exhibition, bears witness to significant  moments, not with judgment or ideology, but with a deep and unflinching empathy for the human condition. Featuring 110 unique photographs, this exhibition is a call not for division, but for togetherness.

name: Unit 13
description: Unit 13 is a space of many parts -  office, workshop, venue, exhibition space, and screening room. It is concieved as a social space in which to collaborate. A place of exchange - both ideas, skills, knowledge, and energy. During the working week we have three architecture practices working from the space - AH A, LSD, and TJA - alongside a revolving exhibition. During the weekend, we have talks.

name: Wolves Lane Horticultural Centre
description: Ever explored an eco-building? Wolves Lane Horticulture centre is home to a thriving 3.5 acre contemporary community food growing space alongside 1970s glasshouses. Visit the cactus and palm house with koi carp alongside a “bale” of terrapins and exotic flora and fauna. The café serves healthy, locally grown produce and the shop will furnish you with plants to take home.
address: Wolves Lane Centre, Wolves Lane, N22 5JD

name: Worlds End Studios
description:
The building of Worlds End Studios started life as a factory manufacturing machines for commercial baking ovens; it burned down and the remains were used as the foundations of what we know today.
Two young architects found the ruined site in 1974. They wanted to create a community workspace geared toward designers, one of the first of its kind, in London.

name: outhouse gallery
description:
outhouse gallery is a small, independent, artist-run creative space located in Brunswick Park, Camberwell. 
As a former public toilet, the gallery's mission is to be open, public and accessible to both facilitators and visitors - from free exhibitions, live performances, and workshops to publishing articles online and in outhouse magazine.
